features.name: share_oc_comments_citing_sources
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments explicitly reference an external source (e.g., study, article, statistic with attribution, book, link, named authority)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own text explicitly references an external source as support (URL/link, named study, article, book, report, statistic attributed to a source, named expert or institution cited as authority). Mere personal experience, unsourced claims, or generic 'studies show' without any identifiable source do not count unless a source is explicitly named or linked. Quoting the OP does not count. Exclude any text announcing OP view change/delta award, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Output = (comments that reference a source) / (total comments), range 0-1. Empty list -> null; malformed -> null. List order carries no meaning.

h0: share_oc_comments_citing_sources has no association with delta.
h1: Higher share_oc_comments_citing_sources is associated with higher probability of delta (OP view change).
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Share chosen as the row-level measure of 'counter-arguments that reference sources'; any/count are alternatives. Comments are unordered, with no timing; conversation is not used. Comments may contain outcome-related text, which is excluded from the semantic judgment. Association only, not causal.
